newsitem.title: UK: UK accountants say no to euro-currency - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK accountants say no to euro-currency - poll.

text.p: Around 80 percent of UK accountants believe it essential that Britain remain part of a tariff-free Europe, but over two-thirds reject the notion of a single currency, according to a poll released on Thursday.

In a survey of over 200 accountants by the UK's Hays Accountancy Personnel and Accountancy Age magazine, only 31 percent supported a single European currency and only 13 percent backed the idea of a federal Europe.

"The survey clearly shows that while support for the UK's existing level of involvement in Europe is strong, there is little enthusiasm for closer monetary union," said Hays Accountancy Personnel managing director Denis Waxman.

The poll said respondents recognised that the UK could lose out if it did not wholeheartedly support Europe, with 65 percent believing London could lose its position as the pre-eminent financial centre in Europe as a result.
Just under half of respondents said the issue of Europe would impact on the way they voted at the next UK general election, which must be held by May next year.
